note: How operators become agents. One invocation of one operator is one agent, created fresh on the operator's own profile (operator.json → resources) with the aliases its Context table declares and nothing else. The orchestrator owns dispatch: it writes the step's input.json and request.md, starts the agent, validates the step (scripts/validate-step.mjs, then the operator's validate.mjs), and follows routing.json to the next operator, user, or external party. It never merges two operators into one agent and never lets an agent start another; a fresh critique agent inside architecture.decide is the one exception, spawned by the orchestrator for that step and given only the step's artifacts.

agent.grants: operator.json → resources.requires, and nothing the profile would otherwise permit
agent.refs: operator.md → Context table (an old-shape package: operator.json → refs), resolved through alias/alias.json; an unlisted location is unreadable
agent.requirements: operator.md → Requirements table; the orchestrator fills defaults and asks a person only for fields whose Default is — or whose value the stop code names
agent.writes: only its own step folder step-N-M/: response.md, data/, artifacts/, output.json; the old shape writes @dynamic/<file> in steps/<n>.<operator.id>/

concurrency.rule: at most maxConcurrentAgents agents at once; steps sharing N run concurrently only when their Writes touch no common alias
concurrency.sharedCheckout: two agents may read one checkout; only one may hold it for writing (backend.implement, fe.source.apply, git.publish are exclusive per checkout)
concurrency.sharedRoot: business.decide is exclusive per businesses root; platform.operate is exclusive per runtime owner

handoff.carrier: output.json fields: kind → file inside the step folder; the next agent's request.md Inputs table points at ../step-N-M/<file>, nearest earlier producer wins
handoff.stop: output.json status blocked with stop = code; errors/ says whether the code terminates or falls back, and routing.json says where a terminated step hands to
handoff.resume: a blocked step re-enters the same operator as a new agent in a new step folder, with resume naming the blocked step and its token

session.manifest: session.json: id, project, startedAt, status (running | blocked | done), chain [["1-1"], ["2-1", "2-2"], ...], steps { "N-M": operatorId }, current, leases { "N-M": agent }
session.step: step-<N>-<M>/ — N is the position in the chain, M the parallel branch
stepLayout: critique.md when the operator has one
session.read: an Input kind resolves to the nearest earlier step whose output.json fields lists it; two producers of one kind in one session (backend.implement then fe.source.apply both produce changes) therefore resolve to the later one unless request.md pins an earlier step
lifecycle: create: the orchestrator writes session.json and takes the leases before the first agent starts
step: each agent gets a fresh step-N-M/ folder with input.json and request.md already written, and writes only there
advance: output.json status done and both validators green; the orchestrator writes the next step's input.json from the Next table and routing.json
block: status blocked keeps the session on disk; the orchestrator asks the person for the field the stop names, then re-enters the operator in step-(N+1)-1 with resume set

done: when routing reaches user or external, or git.publish emits done, the orchestrator releases the leases and deletes the session folder; what survives is what the steps published (commits, business heads, UAT pairs, remote runs) and any audit record the owner copies out first
